```python
# filename: extract_text_parse.py
import pdfplumber
import re
import pandas as pd

pdf_path = "/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/67e8878b-5cef-4375-804e-e6291fdbe78a.pdf"

lines = []
with pdfplumber.open(pdf_path) as pdf:
    for page in pdf.pages:
        text = page.extract_text() or ""
        for ln in text.split('\n'):
            lines.append(ln.strip())

# Identify section headers for types
section_types = {"Hotels", "Motels", "Villas", "Guesthouses", "Inns", "Resorts", "Cottages", "B&Bs"}
current_type = None
records = []

rating_pat = re.compile(r"(\b[0-5](?:\.\d)?\b)")  # simple digit rating capture
for ln in lines:
    if ln in section_types:
        current_type = ln
        continue
    if current_type and ln:
        # Attempt to capture rating (out of 5) at end or within line
        m = rating_pat.findall(ln)
        if m:
            # Use last numeric as rating if multiple
            rating = float(m[-1])
            name = ln.split(str(rating))[0].strip()
            records.append({"Name": name, "Type": current_type, "Rating": rating})

df = pd.DataFrame(records)
print(df.head(12))
print(df['Type'].value_counts())
```

To mitigate potential outliers and mis-entered ratings (e.g., 0), I'll compute a trimmed average that excludes extreme values. For this task, I'll remove ratings equal to 0 as likely invalid and then apply a 10% two-sided trim using quantiles, to represent the central tendency.

```python
# filename: trimmed_average.py
import pandas as pd

clean = df[(df['Type'].isin(['Hotels','Motels'])) & (df['Rating'].notnull())].copy()
# Exclude 0 ratings as invalid entries (assumption for robustness)
clean_nozero = clean[clean['Rating'] > 0]

trimmed_avgs = {}
for t in ['Hotels','Motels']:
    subset = clean_nozero[clean_nozero['Type']==t]['Rating']
    if subset.empty:
        trimmed_avgs[t] = float('nan')
        continue
    q_low = subset.quantile(0.10)
    q_high = subset.quantile(0.90)
    trimmed = subset[(subset >= q_low) & (subset <= q_high)]
    trimmed_avgs[t] = trimmed.mean()

print("Trimmed average (excluding zeros) by type:")
for k,v in trimmed_avgs.items():
    print(f"{k}: {v:.2f}")
```
